name: Grawa-Wasserfall
kurzbeschreibung: The Grawa-Wasserfall in Neustift im Stubaital: at 85 m the widest waterfall in the Eastern Alps, 180 m drop, WildeWasserWeg and healing spray inhalation.
beschreibung:
Overview

The monumental Grawa-Wasserfall in the rear Stubaital within the municipal area of Neustift im Stubaital is a natural monument of superlatives. With a cascade width of an impressive 85 metres, it is considered the widest waterfall in the entire Eastern Alps. Fed by the massive glacier ice of the Sulzenauferner in the Stubaier Alpen, the roaring waters of the Sulzaubach plunge 180 vertical metres into the valley across two powerful tiers. Nestled in primeval Swiss pine and larch forest, this natural spectacle, declared a protected natural monument in 1979, forms the indisputable centerpiece of the acclaimed WildeWasserWeg.

Natural Phenomenon & Health Benefits

This geological monument formed during the last Ice Age as the deep glacial U-shaped valleys of the Stubaital were carved out. When the ice-cold glacial meltwater crashes against the hard granite-gneiss rocks, the water is atomized into microscopic droplets. A pioneering clinical study by the Paracelsus Medizinischen Privatuniversität Salzburg (PMU), led by Univ.-Doz. Dr. Arnulf Hartl, scientifically substantiated the extraordinary curative power of this natural phenomenon: mechanical atomization creates an extremely high concentration of negatively charged ions and respirable nano-aerosols. Spending just one hour in the spray zone demonstrably doubles the clearance and self-cleaning rate of the upper respiratory tract, providing noticeable relief for asthma, bronchitis, and hay fever. To experience this curative microclimate to the fullest, the Tourismusverband Stubai built the Grawa-Observatorium: an award-winning, wave-shaped wooden platform situated right at the foot of the thundering cascades, featuring comfortable Swiss pine loungers that invite visitors to relax and consciously inhale.

Visit & Arrival

The Grawa-Wasserfall and the observatory are accessible year-round, 365 days a year, 24 hours a day, and are completely free of charge (€0.00 admission). The most rewarding time to visit is during the summer months from May to October, when glacial melting peaks and the cascades thunder with maximum water volume. In winter, the waterfall transforms into a colossal sculpture of blue ice. Public transport arrival: Take VVT bus line 590 (Stubaitalbus) from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof or Fulpmes every half hour directly to the Neustift i. St. Grawa Wasserfall stop (buses halt right at the trailhead). By car: Brennerautobahn A13 to the Schönberg/Stubaital exit, then follow the B183 Stubaitalstraße through Neustift and Ranalt to the hiker car park at the Grawa Alm (paid parking spaces available directly on site).

Tips

Unlike many Alpine ravines, the Grawa-Wasserfall offers exemplary barrier-free accessibility: from the bus stop and the Grawa Alm, a wide, flat, and finely graveled walking path leads in just about 400 metres (approx. 10 minutes on foot) to the viewing platform; the entire wooden deck of the Grawa-Observatorium is stepless and fully accessible for wheelchairs and strollers. The adjacent, 400-year-old Grawa Alm also features a wheelchair-accessible restroom and sunny outdoor seating. Pack a windproof and water-resistant jacket, as the curative mist gently drifts across the relaxation loungers depending on wind conditions.
oeffnungszeiten: Ganzjährig frei zugänglich (Beste Besuchszeit Mai bis Oktober)
